android.desc: Connect to your computers completely privately from anywhere over peer-to-peer VPN with zero network configuration! Sign up for Morpheusly by visiting www.morpheusly.com to Download and Get Started. Need bVNC on iOS or Mac OS X? Now available at https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/bvnc-pro/id1506461202 Thank you for supporting my work and GPL open-source software by donating! Please also rate my application, and tell everyone about it! Release notes: https://github.com/iiordanov/remote-desktop-clients/blob/master/bVNC/CHANGELOG-bVNC Older versions: https://github.com/iiordanov/remote-desktop-clients/releases Report bugs: https://github.com/iiordanov/remote-desktop-clients/issues If you have questions, please don't post a negative review, rather, ask your question on the forum so everybody benefits: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/bvnc-ardp-aspice-opaque-remote-desktop-clients Check out my RDP Client, aRDP https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.iiordanov.freeaRDP For Proxmox and oVirt, get Opaque https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.undatech.opaque bVNC is a secure, open source VNC client. GPL licensed, basically identical to the "non-pro" version, $5. I don't know how well that works out for them, but I think it is a model worth supporting.

See also:

https://games.slashdot.org/story/11/11/25/2217247/valves-gabe-newell-on-piracy-its-not-a-pricing-problem
quotes.story_title: Why Open Source Misses the Point of Free Software (2007)

quotes.text:
I think that this is in large part due to hurdles of paying for software easily.

For example

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.iiordanov.freebVNC&hl=en_US

and

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.iiordanov.bVNC&hl=en_US

are the same GPL licensed software either gratis or for $5. Just buying it via the store is straightforward instead of figuring out where the homepage is, finding a donate button, entering credit card details... .

Having more non-gratis but free software would be a good thing

https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/selling.en.html
